# Project plan

## Start-up phase

Month 1 (January 2027): create the `tidyvar` repository with an MIT license, a code of conduct, issue templates and GitHub Actions for R CMD check on Linux, macOS and Windows, and add it to r-universe. Open the design note for the variant table and the provenance attribute as a discussion for tidyomics and VariantAnnotation maintainers. Extract the VRS Allele test data from the specification repository into the test suite. Assemble three de-identified rare disease variant tables from the lab as test cases. Reporting: a progress note each month and a blog post at each milestone.

## Technical delivery

| Milestone | Deliverables | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| M1, table and identity. January to March 2027. | `variant_table()`, `read_variants()`, `normalize_variants()`, `vrs_id()`, `as_vranges()`, `as_variant_table()`. Release 0.1 on r-universe. Announcement post. | Every VRS Allele test case yields the identifier the specification lists. A VCF round-trips through VRanges with no lost records. The lab's three tables load and get identifiers. |
| M2, adapters and provenance. April to June 2027. | `annotate_variants()` with six adapters: ClinVar, gnomAD, Ensembl VEP, MyVariant.info, UniProt, local file. `provenance()`. Adapter authoring guide. Release 0.2. | Each adapter has a recorded-response test. Every annotated column carries source, release, retrieval time and query. One real case review in the lab runs on tidyvar end to end. |
| M3, documentation and submission. July to August 2027. | Two vignettes: germline triage of a rare disease trio, and a ClinVar against gnomAD frequency check. pkgdown site. Bioconductor submission opened. Delivery post. | Vignettes run in CI without network, from recorded responses. The submission issue is open on the Bioconductor contributions tracker. |

Target dates: 0.1 by 31 March 2027, 0.2 by 30 June 2027, Bioconductor submission by 31 August 2027.

Failure modes and recovery. If an API changes, the recorded-response tests keep the package testable and a fix is confined to one adapter. If VRS normalization has edge cases we do not anticipate, the specification's test data exposes them, and we file failures upstream and mark the case as unsupported. If Bioconductor review takes longer than the grant, the milestone is the submission, not the acceptance, and the package stays installable from r-universe. If dissertation work takes time from one of us, the other covers the milestone.

## Other aspects

License: MIT for code, CC BY 4.0 for documentation. Code on GitHub, binaries on r-universe, documentation as a pkgdown site. Announcement at 0.1 and a delivery post at the end, both offered to the R Consortium blog. Talks at the Birmingham (Alabama) R Users Group, at the UAB Center for Computational Genomics and Data Science seminar, and submissions to BioC 2027 and useR! 2027 at our own cost. Issues and pull requests open from day one.

## Budget & funding plan

Total request: 10,000 USD. All of it is labor at 50 USD per hour, 200 hours, managed by the lead. No hardware, cloud, travel or fees.

| Milestone | Hours | Amount (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| M1, table and identity | 80 | 4,000 |
| M2, adapters and provenance | 80 | 4,000 |
| M3, documentation and submission | 40 | 2,000 |

If the ISC funds part of the request, M1 stands alone and delivers the VRS identifiers and the VRanges bridge, which are the two parts nobody else provides.
